According to the Financial Times, the latest court documents show that OpenAI is disappointed with the adoption of ChatGPT via Apple Intelligence, stating that the integration performed "far below expectations" after its launch in 2024. Details below.

OpenAI Requests Court Ruling Before Trial

In August 2025, Elon Musk stated that X, now merged into SpaceXAI, would sue Apple and OpenAI over alleged collusion to suppress competitors in the AI space. The dispute stems from OpenAI's deal with Apple to integrate ChatGPT into Apple Intelligence and Siri.

When the lawsuit was filed, it went beyond Musk's initial public complaint regarding App Store rankings. X and SpaceXAI also accused Apple of attempting to curb the development of "super apps," including X's efforts to transform itself into an "everything app."

In the weeks and months that followed, the involved companies filed briefs, allegations, and defences with the court. Apple and OpenAI have consistently argued that the deal is not an exclusive partnership as alleged in the complaint; court documents have also revealed new details about how the collaboration operates behind the scenes.

One such detail was exposed in a filing OpenAI submitted today. As first reported by the Financial Times, OpenAI "said it was disappointed by how little interest Apple generated among iPhone users after the two struck a deal in 2024 to power 'Apple Intelligence' with ChatGPT."

The report cites:

Wednesday's court documents state that when the 2024 deal was struck, OpenAI anticipated a "halo effect" from Apple's promotion and brand association, expecting more subscriptions from Apple Intelligence users. However, one month after the ChatGPT integration launched, the feature "had a seemingly slow start," and OpenAI subsequently lowered its weekly active user growth forecast. The documents state that by summer 2025, "it had become clear that Apple's integration of ChatGPT was seriously underperforming."

The report notes that today's filing contains multiple redacted portions of conversation content, but the unredacted portions show that OpenAI executives were concerned Apple might "want to accelerate" efforts to identify another AI partner.

When Apple Intelligence was first announced in 2024, Craig Federighi said in an interview that Apple ultimately wanted to give users the ability to choose between different AI models, specifically mentioning Google Gemini as a potential future integration option.

That particular partnership did not materialise, but Apple has since turned to Google's Gemini model to help power the new Siri AI, while Xcode has also been expanded to support coding agents from Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI.

Returning to today's filing, the Financial Times notes that the documents also mention that Apple's approach to rolling out ChatGPT may be one reason for the slow adoption rate, since the integration is opt-in by default.

Finally, according to Reuters, OpenAI is also arguing that SpaceX's recent securities filings undermine SpaceXAI's claim that the Apple deal harms competition. OpenAI states in the filing that SpaceX's IPO registration statement is "replete with disclosures that are the polar opposite of the competitive harm alleged in the lawsuit."

Based on these grounds, OpenAI is asking Judge Mark Pittman to rule in its favour on SpaceXAI's antitrust allegations before trial. The case is currently scheduled for trial in January.
